sources.excerpt: Keeley Electronics Announces The Tone Workstation: A Modular Analog Pedalboard Revolution | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / gear reviews gear reviews Keeley Electronics Announces The Tone Workstation: A Modular Analog Pedalboard Revolution By Liam Carter July 15, 2026 What Is the Tone Workstation? Keeley Electronics’ Tone Workstation is not another multi-effects unit or digital processor. It is a purpose-built, analog-centric hardware platform that redefines how guitarists and bass players manage complex pedal configurations. Unveiled at the 2024 NAMM Show in Anaheim, the Tone Workstation is a 3U (5.25-inch tall) 19-inch rack-mounted device weighing 12.8 pounds and measuring 17.25 × 13.5 × 6.5 inches (W × D × H). Unlike conventional loop switchers such as the Boss ES-8 or TC Electronic Nexus, the Tone Workstation integrates analog signal path control, real-time voltage-based modulation routing, and built-in power regulation into a single chassis — all without digitizing the audio path. The core architecture centers on four fully independent stereo channels, each with its own dedicated input/output pair, buffered bypass circuitry, and assignable expression CV (control voltage) output. Each channel supports up to two analog effect modules — meaning the system can host up to eight discrete analog pedals simultaneously while maintaining true analog signal integrity from input to output. Keeley confirmed zero digital conversion occurs in the audio path; all switching, gain staging, and level balancing happen entirely in the analog domain using discrete JFETs and low-noise op-amps (Texas Instruments OPA2134 and OPA1612). Crucially, the Tone Workstation does not require external power supplies for connected pedals. Its internal 12V DC power distribution system delivers regulated, filtered, and isolated outputs: eight 9V DC (center-negative) ports rated at 300mA each, two 12V DC (center-negative) ports at 500mA, and one 18V DC port at 400mA — sufficient to power high-current devices like the Strymon Big Sky, Empress Effects Reverb, or Walrus Audio Mako Series without noise bleed or voltage sag. Hardware Design & Physical Interface Keeley’s industrial design team collaborated with aerospace-grade enclosure manufacturer Bud Industries to fabricate the chassis from 1.2mm cold-rolled steel with powder-coated matte black finish. Front-panel controls consist of 16 tactile, gold-plated Alps RK09K rotary encoders (four per channel), eight LED-lit footswitches (two per channel), and dual high-resolution OLED displays (128 × 64 pixels each) showing real-time signal metrics including input/output level (−40dBV to +10dBV), channel mute status, and expression pedal position (0–100%). Each channel features three physical I/O connectors: a ¼” TRS input, a ¼” TRS output, and a 3.5mm stereo expression input. Rear-panel connectivity expands functionality significantly: two balanced XLR inputs/outputs (switchable between line-level and instrument-level via rear DIP switches), MIDI IN/OUT/THRU ports compliant with MIDI 1.0 specification, USB-C host port for firmware updates (not audio streaming), and an Ethernet port supporting OSC (Open Sound Control) over LAN for integration with Ableton Live, MainStage, or custom control software. Power Architecture Deep Dive The internal power supply uses a toroidal transformer coupled with six independent linear regulators — one per 9V rail plus dedicated regulators for 12V and 18V outputs. Ripple suppression measures below 150µV RMS across all rails, verified by Keysight DSOX2004A oscilloscope testing at full load. This exceeds industry benchmarks set by Voodoo Lab Ground Control Pro (220µV) and Eventide UltraSwitch (180µV). All power outputs are individually fused with slow-blow 350mA ceramic fuses, preventing cascade failures. sources.excerpt: Keeley | Tone Workstation Multi-Effects - Sugaree Licks Skip to content Menu Cart Sugaree Licks Cart Search All Amps All Pedals All Guitars Songs Albums Artists Submit Submit A Song Add An Album To Sugaree Licks Add An Artist To Sugaree Licks Equipment For Sale Clearance Pedals Amps All Amps Top Amps Submit An Amp Pedals All Pedals Top Pedals Submit A Pedal Guitars All Guitars Top Guitars Submit A Guitar Manufacturers All Manufacturers Submit A Manufacturer GET Guitar Equipment Terminology Chords Guitar Chords A Guitar Chords B Guitar Chords C Guitar Chords D Guitar Chords E Guitar Chords F Guitar Chords G SHOP Widgets User Account Username or Email Password Remember Me or REGISTER Close Menu Close Cart   Keeley | Tone Workstation Multi-Effects by Sweetwater Website Link Keeley Website Link Model Number or Name: Tone Workstation Boost Compression Multi-Effect Overdrive Circuit Type: Analog Electrical Components: JFET Transistor Original Price: $299 Excellent Used Price: $230 Year Released: 2015 Alternate Version(s) No Alternate Versions Listed Ten years ago we invented and built a small batch of the Tone Workstation, which then moved into the hands of famous players and collectors. John Mayer recently took two of the originals out on the Dead & Company tour. For 2016 it’s more than a re-release; it’s a completely new, re-engineered workstation. The Keeley team of engineers and designers have upgraded the tone, enhanced the features, and reduced the size to now fit on anyone’s board. Introducing the Tone Workstation The front end of your signal chain–this is where your tone develops. The first stage of amplification is critical for a sound that has clarity and delivers expressive tone. Compression, Drive, Overdrive, Boost: you get it all here. The Tone Workstation is designed to be the first stage in your pedal board. It may even be the only pedal you bring to a gig. And we designed it that way. Starting with the classic Keeley Compressor, you can build a nice, thick tone full of sustain. Adjust the Sustain control for increased compression or squeeze. As you add sustain, your notes will ring out longer. The Blend control allows for a Manhattan-style compression, keeping the sound lively and crisp as you blend in your natural guitar tone. The Blend control is perfect for adding a little bit of bite back in with high output pickups or humbuckers. In addition, the Treble Boost switch can be engaged to further increase the treble and sparkle into the signal when using lots of compression. When the Blend is set completely CCW, you get only compressed signal out. Then, as you turn up the Blend, you blend in more and more of your original signal, all the way to a 50/50 ratio. The attack and release times are pre-set in this compressor and are set for use with humbuckers or single coils. Next up is the 1962/Katana Boost section, because the Keeley Workstation gives you plenty of options for your core tone. With the 62/Katana channel, you can select a sound with just the right amount of break up. Or use it in Boost mode, for that clean, pushed amp-style overdrive. First, the 1962 is our British amp-style overdrive, which is full and even sounding with a moderate amount of crunch. Based on the famous Blues Breaker, the 1962 stage has been amplified by our Katana Boost on either side, adding tube-like saturation with our JFET valve simulation. But, decide you just want the famous Katana Clean push? No worries. Just a flick of the switch and you have it: pure clean, tube tone. In the Katana Mode, only the volume works; the Tone and Drive are disabled. It’s a clean sound people say you just can’t turn off. Last in the chain is our renowned Red Dirt overdrive. You get 15 years of modding tube screamers distilled into one toneful circuit. Also featuring our JFET front end, the Red Dirt has the perfect amount of crucial midrange coupled with the option to go all the way from clean and clear to super-saturated gain, times two!
